plain: The Majestic 12 papers are a set of typed pages that call themselves a secret briefing for President-elect Eisenhower, and they say a flying saucer crashed in 1947 and its wreckage was recovered. Michels calls it 'easily the most controversial' document in UFO circles. According to the note on where it comes from, the briefing came to light on a roll of 35mm film that a man named Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his home in Burbank in 1984. Shandera studied it with William Moore and the UFO researcher Stanton Friedman, and it was made public in 1987. The papers are headed 'OPERATION MAJESTIC-12 PRELIMINARY BRIEFING FOR PRESIDENT-ELECT EISENHOWER', carry the date 18 November 1952, and include a memo said to be from Truman to Defense Secretary Forrestal dated 24 September 1947. Page 3 says that on 7 July 1947 'a secret operation was begun to assure recovery of the wreckage of this object for scientific study' and that 'four small human-like beings had apparently ejected from the craft'. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower libraries report finding nothing. The FBI's copies are marked 'BOGUS' by hand, and they record that the Air Force's investigators called it 'fabricated'. The writer Philip Klass called the Truman memo a fraud, and Friedman judged the papers 'almost certainly genuine'. Relaying Friedman, Michels says that if the document is real it proves a saucer crashed and was recovered, and that a man named Donald Menzel was rumoured to be in the group. That holds only as far as the papers are genuine, and their origin is exactly what is in dispute. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says on the show that he is 'particularly fond of' the Eisenhower briefing, and he names Forrestal and Walter B. Smith among those tied to it.

discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". The paper is headed "OPERATION MAJESTIC-12 PRELIMINARY BRIEFING FOR PRESIDENT-ELECT EISENHOWER" and "DOCUMENT PREPARED 18 NOVEMBER, 1952", and its page 3 says that on 07 July 1947 "a secret operation was begun to assure recovery of the wreckage of this object for scientific study" and that "four small human-like beings had apparently ejected from the craft at some point before it exploded". The tellers describe the paper as it describes itself; that a saucer crashed and its wreckage was recovered is established only as far as the paper is genuine, which is the step its provenance leaves in dispute.
